puzzle.prompt:
Solve this number-constraint puzzle.

Unknown variables: D, F, I, J, L, N, O, Q, R, S, T, V, W, Y.

Rules:
- Each unknown is an integer from 1 to 5.
- Satisfy every remaining-value constraint below.
- A variable has the same value wherever it appears.
- Numbers may be reused in different groups; within a listed group each listed number appears exactly once.

Remaining-value constraints (fixed values have already been removed):
- D must be 2, in some order (each listed number exactly once).
- F, I, J must be 2, 4, 5, in some order (each listed number exactly once).
- L, N, O must be 1, 3, 4, in some order (each listed number exactly once).
- Q, R, S, T must be 1, 2, 4, 5, in some order (each listed number exactly once).
- V, W, Y must be 1, 4, 5, in some order (each listed number exactly once).
- F must be 4, in some order (each listed number exactly once).
- L, Q, V must be 2, 3, 5, in some order (each listed number exactly once).
- R, W must be 1, 4, in some order (each listed number exactly once).
- D, I, N, S must be 1, 2, 4, 5, in some order (each listed number exactly once).
- J, O, T, Y must be 1, 2, 4, 5, in some order (each listed number exactly once).

Inequalities (fixed values have already been substituted):
- Y < 3
- N < I
- 2 < V
- O < T
- L < 5

The puzzle has exactly one solution. Reason through the constraints and check your assignment.
Finish your reasoning with </thinking>, then give the unknown values inside <answer> and </answer>.
Write one NAME=number assignment for each unknown, in the order listed above. Separate assignments with spaces.
Only output the unknowns. Fixed values are supplied by the environment.
